subject: Information Theory
title: Codons and Redundancy
description: Learn Codons and Redundancy in one minute.

hook.text: There are 64 possible three-letter codons but only 20 amino acids. The genetic code has massive built-in redundancy.

buildup.text: Multiple codons map to the same amino acid. Leucine has six codons. Methionine has one. It's an uneven code.

discovery.text: This redundancy protects against mutations. Many single-base changes still produce the same amino acid.

twist.text: The code isn't random—similar codons code for chemically similar amino acids. Errors degrade gracefully.

climax.text: Information theory calls this error tolerance. Nature designed a code where most point mutations cause minimal damage.

punchline.text: 64 codons, 20 amino acids. Redundancy protects life.

quiz.question: Why does the genetic code have 64 codons for only 20 amino acids?
